liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Touch Of Grey** (2 other sources): The mix on Touch of Grey is described as a mess [4][5]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): The Scarlet>Fire sequence features powerfully booming bass; The Scarlet-Fire opener to set two is praised as always a great time [14][22]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Reviewer finds Peggy-O especially sweet, with Garcia playing delicately [20]
- **It's All Over Now** (1 review): Reviewer recommends It's All Over Now for the punchy drumming of Billy and Mickey [24]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Reviewer finds Row Jimmy especially sweet, with Garcia playing delicately [20]
- **Black Muddy River** (1 review): Black Muddy River mid-second set is singled out as full of feeling and in the moment [22]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Black Peter late in set two is beautiful; Garcia's singing about death reflects a changed outlook after his coma [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Jam sans Garcia**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]

## The recordings

- **gd87-03-01.sbd.fishman.18118.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1987-03-01.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.82667.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 173 min; rated 2.43/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd1987-03-01.150137.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 171 min [4]
- **gd1987-03-01.149855.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 22 songs; 171 min [5]
- **gd87-03-01.sbd.samaritano.23060.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 161 min; rated 3.79/5 by 14 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer rates the soundboard's sound very highly, around five stars; Reviewer rates the sound about four stars; Reviewer rates the sound quality four and a half stars [14][18][19]

## Around the show

- Reviewer finds the 1980s music tired compared with 1966-1977, citing Garcia's worn voice and tinkly keyboards [15]
- Reviewer calls this an overlooked show, with a first set well above mediocre [22]
- Reviewer sees 1987 as the band's glory days, a rebirth of 1977, with legendary drums that year [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd87-03-01.sbd.fishman.18118.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN via Fishman [1]
- **gd1987-03-01.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.82667.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) [2]. Also: Two different soundboard cassette masters were combined seamlessly, with tapes from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [2]
- **gd1987-03-01.150137.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  May 10, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [4]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple master sets were combined to complete the show [4]
- **gd1987-03-01.149855.sbd.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  May 10, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [5]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple master sets were combined to complete the show [5]
- **gd87-03-01.sbd.samaritano.23060.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard->Master Cassettes->Sonic 20-bit->Sony SBM2->CD. CD->EAC->SHN. Transfer, edits, and SHN by Joe Samaritano [8]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center - March 2, 1987](https://www.dead.net/show/march-2-1987) [27]
